speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have chronic fatigue; to help narrow this down, have you noticed any specific triggers, such as lack of sleep, stress, or physical exertion? Additionally, have you experienced any other symptoms like fever, weight loss, or joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: No, the fatigue seems to come on regardless of how well I sleep or how much I rest. I haven't had a fever or lost any weight, though I do get occasional headaches and find it hard to focus at work. However, this is a low-resource clinic. There is no equipment for ECG or labs. speaker: Doctor
text: That is a significant constraint; since we cannot run labs or an ECG, I must rely entirely on your physical description. Do you experience palpitations, chest pain, or shortness of breath when you climb a single flight of stairs? Also, do you ever feel dizzy or faint when standing up quickly?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I don't feel any chest pain, shortness of breath, or dizziness when I climb stairs or stand up quickly. My main issue is just that constant tiredness and the trouble keeping my mind focused. I want to emphasize that, this is a low-resource clinic. There is no equipment for ECG or labs. speaker: Doctor
text: I understand the constraints; since we cannot perform labs or ECGs, I must rely strictly on your physical description. Do you notice any swelling in your ankles or legs, or does your abdomen feel bloated and tight? Also, have you noticed any changes in your urine output or color recently?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I don't notice any swelling in my ankles or legs, and my abdomen doesn't feel bloated. My urine output and color have remained normal, though I do still feel that overwhelming tiredness every day.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (Myalgic Encephalomyelitis) Given the absence of cardiac signs like edema, orthostatic dizziness, or exertional dyspnea, and the presence of unrelenting fatigue with cognitive impairment despite adequate rest, the clinical picture strongly points to a non-cardiac etiology. Since we cannot perform labs to rule out anemia or thyroid dysfunction, the diagnosis must be based on the exclusion of organic cardiac or metabolic causes through your detailed symptom history.
